feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV with clear senior-level positioning in digital communications and strategy. It shows progression, relevant technical depth, and solid scope, but impact would be stronger with more quantified outcomes and less repetition across skills sections.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression within one organization, culminating in leadership and consulting roles; this supports credibility and growth.  
- Strong domain alignment: digital strategy, Drupal/web modernization, analytics, multimedia, and advocacy communications are consistently reinforced.  
- Writing is polished and professional overall, with good clarity and a modern, achievement-oriented tone.

1. Top improvements  
- Add more measurable results beyond scope metrics: include outcomes such as email growth, engagement improvements, traffic gains, conversion lifts, cost savings, or efficiency gains.  
- Reduce redundancy: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap significantly; consolidate to tighten structure and save space.  
- Minor writing/style fixes: “12 years experience” should be “12 years’ experience” or “more than 12 years of experience”; maintain consistent serial comma usage (“web, content, email, social media, and multimedia” vs later lists without it); “French (A2/Learning)” is stylistically awkward—use “French (A2, learning)” or “French (basic working proficiency).”
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary with clear seniority and scope, but it reads slightly generic and repeats themes already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills. Tightening the language and adding a sharper value proposition will improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience” for cleaner style and correct grammar.
- Lead with your niche: digital strategy and communications leadership for mission-driven/public-sector organizations.
- Replace broad phrases like “expert in” with more specific strengths tied to outcomes, such as CMS modernization, cross-channel operations, and accessible advocacy/policy content.
- Keep it to 2 sentences to make the header punchier and avoid listing every channel already detailed elsewhere.

Possible rewrite:
Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience leading web, content, email, social media, and multimedia programs for mission-driven organizations. Specializes in cross-channel communications, CMS modernization, and scalable editorial workflows, with a strong track record translating policy and technical issues into clear, accessible advocacy content.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications,” “workflow/systems,” and “advocacy messaging” are repeated in Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block is broad and overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. Tightening the phrasing and emphasizing higher-value leadership capabilities will make it more distinctive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace generic terms with sharper, senior-level language: “Multi-channel communication” → “Cross-channel communications leadership”; “Web & CMS administration” → “Web platform governance & CMS management.”
- Group related items to reduce list fatigue and improve clarity: strategy/governance, platforms/workflows, analytics, stakeholder communications, multimedia.
- Use parallel noun phrases throughout for style consistency; avoid mixing functions (“administration”) with outcomes (“transformation”).
- Suggested version: Digital strategy & platform modernization • Cross-channel communications leadership • Web platform governance & CMS management • Editorial workflow & content operations design • Analytics, reporting & performance insights • Workflow architecture & systems improvement • Stakeholder & cross-functional coordination • Policy & advocacy communications • Multimedia, livestream & event production

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Repeats several ideas already covered in the header and Topline Skills, especially digital strategy, advocacy messaging, analytics, and multimedia.
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” overlaps with Soft Skills; consider dropping it here if space is tight.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with good scope, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the NACo roles below. Tighten it around consultant-level outcomes, platform modernization, and the AI/search work.

Suggested edit
- Recast into 3–4 impact bullets starting with outcomes: “Advising NACo on enterprise digital strategy, content operations, and web modernization for member-facing communications.”
- Combine overlapping execution bullets: “Built Drupal campaign experiences, including microsites, modular storytelling components, and downloadable toolkits; provided front-end/CMS implementation and troubleshooting for public-facing properties.”
- Elevate systems/governance language: “Designed cross-channel workflows, analytics, and governance practices to improve coordination across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Make the AI work the capstone and quantify if possible: “Leading an AI-enabled search initiative spanning retrieval strategy, structured content design, and discovery UX for complex policy/member content.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “digital strategy, content operations, governance, analytics” repeats the Director of Digital Media entry; emphasize advisory/consulting scope and new initiatives instead.
- Microsite/campaign examples also appear in Recent Projects; keep this item high-level and outcome-focused.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It should be tightened to emphasize outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management points already covered in adjacent NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper scope/outcome line: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function, leading web modernization, analytics, governance, multimedia operations, and budget oversight across web, email, social, and video.”
- Make bullets more results-led: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Add measurable impact where missing: quantify email/social growth, video output, cost savings from the in-house studio, reporting speed, stakeholder adoption, or governance efficiency.
- Tighten generic phrasing: replace “Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels…” with a specific achievement tied to reach, engagement, or campaign performance.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed web, email, social, and video” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this entry focused on enterprise leadership, platform modernization, and systems.
- Video-program language may duplicate older NACo entries; emphasize building the studio and scaling in-house production capacity instead.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry reads generic and overlaps with the more senior NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and quantify scale so it shows clear growth into the Director role.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite the lead to emphasize ownership and scope: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social and video, scaling editorial coordination and advocacy messaging for a national public-sector membership audience.”
- Tighten bullets around concrete outputs: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet more outcome-oriented: “Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “helped improve” with stronger ownership: “Built more consistent editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Strengthened editorial planning…” and “improved…publishing workflows” may duplicate governance/operations points in the Director role; combine or sharpen this entry toward hands-on execution.
- Weekly video updates also appear in the 2015–2018 role; distinguish this as scaling/formalizing the series, not launching it.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this item overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent NACo roles. Tighten it to emphasize senior-level leadership scope and avoid generic phrasing like “audience-focused content planning.”

Suggested edit:
- Replace with sharper, less repetitive language:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial governance and content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy communications
- Content strategy for complex, high-volume organizations
- Consider swapping “Multi-channel” to “Cross-channel” for a more modern, executive tone.
- Replace “messaging” with “communications” to sound broader and more senior.
- If space allows, make one line outcome-oriented, e.g. “Digital strategy for high-volume public-sector platforms” to reinforce scale already proven in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Editorial systems and governance” closely duplicates Core Competencies: “Digital governance & editorial systems.”
- “Audience-focused content planning” is vague and partially repeats experience bullets on storytelling, editorial coordination, and campaign planning.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads like a raw tool list and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. For a topline skills item, emphasize higher-value capabilities tied to recent Drupal modernization and AI/search work, not every platform.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools to capability clusters: “Drupal & CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations & workflow automation • Airtable-based content systems • AI-enabled search experiences”
- Put the strongest, most recent differentiators first: Drupal, CMS modernization, AI-enabled search, then integrations/automation.
- Remove lower-signal platforms unless required by the role; WordPress, SharePoint, and Power Pages are better left to “Technical + IT.”
- If space allows, sharpen wording to outcomes-oriented phrasing: “Drupal platform delivery,” “CMS modernization,” “search and discovery experiences,” “content operations automation.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates the “Technical + IT” platform lists; keep this section strategic and let the technical section carry the full inventory.
- “Workflow automation” and “AI-enabled search experiences” also echo Core Competencies; use tighter phrasing here to avoid repetition.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for the recent Director/Consultant work, but it reads as a generic tool list. It would be stronger if framed around outcomes and trimmed to avoid overlap with the separate “Technical + IT” analytics section.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Analytics, Reporting & Optimization**
- Replace the list with tighter, impact-oriented phrasing: **GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI and Microsoft Clarity • Analytics infrastructure and dashboard development • KPI framework design and leadership reporting • SEO, performance analysis and conversion optimization**
- Group tools first, then capabilities; this makes the section feel more senior than a software inventory.
- If you have metrics, reflect them elsewhere in recent roles (e.g., “expanded analytics infrastructure supporting reporting for a 10,000+ page site and 3.5M annual page views”).

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates **Core Competencies: Analytics and reporting infrastructure** and **Technical + IT: Data, Analytics & Optimization**.
- Consider keeping Topline Skills strategic/capability-focused and leaving the full tool list to Technical + IT.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill area, but this item is too generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and the Technical + IT “Multimedia & Creative Tools” section. It should emphasize delivery capability and scope rather than listing basic production tasks.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe toward outcomes and operating level: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • In-house studio operations • PTZ/multi-camera production systems • Virtual event technical execution”
- Replace “Video production and editing” with a more senior phrase like “Broadcast-quality video production” or “End-to-end video production” to better match Director-level experience.
- Change “Livestreaming” to “Livestream and hybrid event delivery” to signal execution in higher-stakes formats.
- If space allows, add scale/context rather than tools: “Studio buildout and operations” or “Recurring advocacy video and event production.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Studio operations” and “PTZ camera systems” are tool-level and may duplicate “Premiere Pro… Livestream studio workflows” in Technical + IT.
- “Multimedia production and livestream operations” already appears in Core Competencies; use sharper wording here to avoid repetition.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant platforms, but this item is too generic and duplicates the stronger “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” skills section. It should either add specificity on level of use or be tightened to emphasize the most current, highest-value platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by relevance/recency: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages** is fine, but consider: **Drupal (enterprise migration, modular builds) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- Add proficiency/context instead of a bare list, e.g. **Enterprise CMS platforms: Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, make Drupal more outcome-linked: **Drupal (10,000+ page migration; microsites; modular content architecture)**
- Keep this item platform-only; leave development skills, integrations, and automation to adjacent technical categories.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps heavily with **Topline Skills → Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; consider removing one or making this version more concise.
- “CMS modernization” already appears elsewhere, so don’t repeat that phrase here unless replacing the other entry.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. For a senior digital leader, this item should emphasize implementation depth and modern tools rather than basic coding labels.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with: “Front-end implementation: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery • Technical integrations: APIs, Google Tag Manager • Lightweight engineering: Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions”
- Drop versioned/basic terms (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless required by the role; they add little at this level.
- Group tools by function to improve scanability and signal applied capability, not just syntax familiarity.
- If accurate, strengthen with scope qualifiers such as “custom front-end fixes,” “serverless scripts,” or “deployment automation” to show practical use.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills.
- GTM also overlaps conceptually with analytics/optimization; keep it here only if positioned as implementation, not reporting.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of systems leadership. Since workflow automation already appears in Core Competencies and Topline Skills, this item should be tighter and more clearly grouped.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe by function, not a long flat list: “Automation & workflow systems: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier; project/work management: Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp; collaboration: Slack, Microsoft Teams.”
- Put the strongest, most relevant tools first: keep Airtable, Power Automate, and Zapier prominent because they align with your recent workflow/operations leadership.
- Standardize naming for professionalism: use “Microsoft Teams” instead of “Teams.”
- If true, add scope in a parenthetical to increase impact, e.g., “used to support cross-department editorial planning, approvals, and reporting workflows.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already appear in Core Competencies and Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same phrasing here.
- Jira/Asana/Trello/Basecamp overlap heavily; if space is tight, keep only the 2–3 most used.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as generic software inventory rather than evidence of email/engagement capability. Since email leadership is already covered in recent NACo roles, this item should stay concise and platform-focused.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Tighten and standardize naming: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add scope rather than more tools: **Enterprise email automation, newsletter operations, audience segmentation**
- Only keep platforms you’ve used meaningfully in recent roles; if one was light exposure, remove it to strengthen credibility

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid repeating newsletter reach or channel leadership here; that impact is already stronger in the 2022–2024 and 2018–2022 NACo roles
- “Multi-channel communications” and email operations already appear in Core Competencies and Work Experience, so this section should remain a clean tools list

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal and useful scope, but the item is still generic and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and emphasize “firsts,” team-building, and channel ownership without repeating website/video points already covered above.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team, improving day-to-day operations across web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Add a second sentence focused on distinct contributions: “Supported a major website refresh, produced recurring livestreams and weekly video content, and helped formalize workflows for multi-channel publishing.”
- Tighten management phrasing: replace “providing day-to-day guidance” with “mentored a digital media associate” or “supervised a digital media associate’s daily work.”
- If possible, add 1–2 metrics: number of livestreams/videos produced, publishing volume, audience growth, or workflow/time savings.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; keep this entry focused on launching/producing the series, not expanding it.
- Website refresh language overlaps with the 2022–2024 redesign; avoid implying ownership of the later enterprise migration.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry with a credible “first podcast” achievement, but it reads generic and overlaps with later multimedia/digital roles. Emphasize the innovation/program support angle and make the podcast launch the clear standout.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground scope and outcome: “Coordinated county innovation and research initiatives that supported NACo program development and policy communications.”
- Tighten the multimedia line: “Produced digital and multimedia content for member-facing communications, including reports, web materials and campaign assets.”
- Make the differentiator sharper: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting and production.”
- If possible, add one metric or concrete output: number of projects supported, episodes produced, stakeholders served, or content formats delivered.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later digital/media roles; keep this item more focused on innovation/research support plus the podcast launch.
- Avoid broad claims about digital leadership here, since stronger, more recent evidence appears in 2015–2024 roles.
